minutes.headline: Superintendent submitted a budget at the 2.5% target with many cuts; a larger restoring budget is promised Feb 28.
minutes.summary: After executive session, many students, parents and teachers spoke against FY25 cuts, especially to the fifth-grade band and music. The superintendent described the cuts in the budget sent to the town manager, a level-service figure and an Esser-cuts-only figure, and said a version restoring some positions would follow. The committee also voted on school choice, the calendar, preschool tuition and donations, and discussed Chapter 76 private school approval.

what_happened.line: The superintendent described a budget sent to the town manager at the 2.5% target, with cuts, and said a recommended budget restoring some cuts will come February 28.
Dozens of students, parents and teachers spoke against FY25 cuts, mostly to fifth-grade band and the music program.
The committee voted on school choice for grade nine, the school calendar, a preschool tuition increase and two donations; vote counts were not audible.
Members showed broad consensus to keep the music service, possibly through before-school instruction or stipends, pending talks with the union.
The business administrator was named to collect Chapter 76 private school approval materials, and the policy goes to the policy subcommittee.

why_it_matters: The February 28 recommendation will show whether fifth-grade band, music and other positions come back, which would raise the school budget's increase above the 2.5% target that residents will be asked to vote on at town meeting.
The level-service and Esser-cuts-only scenarios show the gap between keeping current services and staying at the target, which is the choice behind the school share of the tax bill.
watch_next: February 28: the superintendent's recommended budget restoring some cuts above the 2.5% target.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the five non-procedural votes (school choice, calendar, preschool tuition, PTO donation, donated days) and on most dollar figures once caption garbling is corrected. The difference to check is that our minutes record two votes the official minutes omit (waiving the 10-minute public comment time and moving the student representative report), and the two describe the paraprofessional negotiating team and Hanscom's title differently.
